subject: CAIQ follow-up: backups, cross-border replication & KMS for Private deployments
messages:

Subject: CAIQ follow-up — backups & cross-border replication

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Our security team is completing the CAIQ and had two specific clarifications before we close the control set: 1) For Private (VPC) deployments and for Dedicated reserved capacity, do backups or disaster-recovery snapshots ever replicate outside the contractually specified region (EU in our case) without explicit customer opt-in? 2) For Private deployments can customers manage their own KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) and have those keys enforced so that Redwood cannot decrypt backups?

We'd appreciate short, definitive answers and any evidence snippets (config example or policy extract) we can paste into the CAIQ. If helpful, Eva from our cloud team is copied to confirm replication mechanics.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Senior Security Manager, MedicaData
attachments: (none)

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@medicadata.com>, Eva Brandt <eva@cloudvendor.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-26T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up — backups & cross-border replication

Hi Maya — great questions. Short answers up front: 

1) Private (VPC) deployments: No. Backups and automated snapshots do NOT replicate outside the customer-designated region unless the customer explicitly requests cross-region replication as part of a documented DR runbook/option. By default data at-rest is kept within the configured region.

2) Customer-managed KMS (BYOK): Yes. For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. When a customer elects BYOK, Redwood does not hold the unencrypted key material and cannot decrypt backup files without customer authorization.

I'm attaching a brief CAIQ-ready excerpt (redwood_caiq_backup_answers_v1.pdf), a high-level replication diagram (s3_replication_architecture_eu.png), and a small key-policy snippet that shows the principal conditions customers can use to restrict Redwood from key usage (kms_key_policy_customer_managed_snippet.txt).

Notes & caveats: 
- Hosted API (Redwood-managed) default behavior is region-local storage per tenant, but we offer optional cross-region snapshot export for DR (explicit contractual option). If a customer enables that export, cross-region copies are created and stored per the agreement.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved instances) operates like Private for backups when network isolation is enforced; however some managed monitoring artifacts may be stored in telemetry pipelines — we can provide a redaction/exclusion map per contract.
- For any cross-region processes we require explicit change-control and documented consent.

If you want, we can produce a one-page control response bundle with CAIQ control IDs mapped to our evidence snippets. Happy to schedule a quick call to walk through the diagrams.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_caiq_backup_answers_v1.pdf; s3_replication_architecture_eu.png; kms_key_policy_customer_managed_snippet.txt

Thanks, Irene — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups so we can close the CAIQ fields verbatim: 

- Can you paste the exact line we should use for CAIQ Questioneering where it asks "Are backups replicated to other regions?" — we'd like a one-sentence answer that we can put in the CAIQ.
- For BYOK: can you confirm whether Redwood requires a key-rotation policy that would allow Redwood to request re-encryption (i.e., do you have any operational playbooks that would cause the customer to re-encrypt backups and, if so, how is that coordinated)?
- Last: any short statement you can provide that says "Redwood does not have the ability to unilaterally decrypt backups protected by customer-managed keys" — that exact language would be great if accurate.

Thanks — if easier, send the edited snippets and we'll paste them in.

—Maya

Folks — forwarding MedicaData's follow-ups. They want CAIQ-ready one-liners and explicit confirmation language. Draft responses below (please review and edit for legal/ops accuracy):

DRAFT_SNIPPETS (please edit):
1) "By default, backups and automated snapshots for Private (VPC) and Dedicated deployments are retained within the customer-specified region and are not replicated to other regions unless the customer explicitly requests cross-region replication as part of a documented disaster recovery configuration."

2) "When configured with customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private deployments, Redwood does not possess the unencrypted key material and cannot decrypt backups without the customer's authorized key usage; Redwood cannot unilaterally decrypt backups protected by customer-managed keys."

3) "Key rotation: Redwood does not mandate customer re-encryption; if a rotation is required by the customer's policy or contractually agreed DR runbook, re-encryption is coordinated with the customer and executed under a documented change control process."

Grace — quick legal check on the BYOK sentence; want to make sure 'cannot unilaterally decrypt' is acceptable phrasing. I'll incorporate edits and send final back to Maya.

Irene

1) Replace sentence 1 with: "By default, backups and automated snapshots for Private (VPC) and Dedicated deployments are retained within the customer-designated region and will not be replicated to other regions unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region replication as part of a documented disaster recovery configuration or contractual option."

2) Replace sentence 2 with: "When customer-managed keys (BYOK) are enabled for Private deployments, customers retain control over key material; Redwood cannot access plaintext backups without explicit customer-granted key usage permissions."
